ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a regular octagon with 8 vertices arranged cyclically, and each pair of adjacent vertices is connected by a side of the octagon. Reasoning: A triangle is formed by choosing 3 of the 8 vertices, so the total number of possible triangles is C(8,3)=56. We want the probability that at least one triangle side is also a side of the octagon, meaning at least two chosen vertices are adjacent on the octagon. Use the complement: count triangles where no two chosen vertices are adjacent around the 8-cycle. For an 8-cycle, the number of 3-subsets with no adjacent vertices is (8/(8-3))*C(8-3,3) = (8/5)*C(5,3) = (8/5)*10 = 16. Therefore, the number of favorable triangles is 56-16=40. The probability is 40/56=5/7.

method.method_draft: Use complementary counting on the vertex choices. Read from the text that 3 vertices are chosen from a regular octagon to form a triangle, and the desired event is that at least one triangle side is an octagon side. Read from the image only the octagon structure: there are 8 vertices arranged cyclically, with adjacent vertices connected by octagon sides. Count all possible triangles as C(8,3)=56. Count the complement: choose 3 vertices with no two adjacent around the octagon. For an 8-cycle, the number of 3-subsets with no adjacent vertices is 8/ (8-3) * C(8-3,3)=8/5*C(5,3)=16, or equivalently count separated cyclic triples. Thus favorable triangles = 56-16=40, so the probability is 40/56=5/7.
